### Q1. BITSAT 2024 (Memory Based Paper 3)

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Level:* `1`

Five identical springs are used in the three configurations as shown in figure. The time periods of vertical oscillations in configurations (a), (b) and (c) are in the ratio.
<img src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/bitsat/q9Z8EDcO7jtbkD6-Rrs7FFufAIz4vFIYoX-vSKBURG4.original.fullsize.png"/>

**Options:**

- **(A)** $1: \sqrt{2}: \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
- **(B)** $2: \sqrt{2}: \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
- **(C)** $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}: 2: 1$
- **(D)** $2: \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}: 1$

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(A) $1: \sqrt{2}: \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$**

**Detailed Solution:**

$\begin{aligned}
& \text { } \quad T_a=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k}} \\
& T_b=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{(k / 2)}} \\
& T_c=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{2 k}} \\
& \therefore \quad T_a: T_b: T_c=1: \sqrt{2}: \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}
\end{aligned}$

</details>

### Q2. BITSAT 2021

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Level:* `1`

Four massless springs whose force constants are $2 k, 2 k, k$ and $2 k$ respectively are attached to a mass $\mathrm{M}$ kept on a frictionless plane (as shown in figure). If the mass $M$ is displaced in the horizontal direction, then the frequency of the system is?

<img src=" data:image/png;base64,">

**Options:**

- **(A)** $\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{4 \mathrm{M}}}$
- **(B)** $\frac{1}{\pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{\mathrm{M}}}$
- **(C)** $\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{7 \mathrm{M}}}$
- **(D)** $\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{7 k}{\mathrm{M}}}$

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(B) $\frac{1}{\pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{\mathrm{M}}}$**

**Detailed Solution:**

The equivalent system is shown in figure.

<img src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/bitsat/42RHMP-yIszBahNNrU3hZoXOKU49eZ4Dbypu4udHdzY.original.fullsize.png">


The equivalent force constant of which $k_{\mathrm{e}}=k+3 k=4 k$ $\therefore \omega=\sqrt{\frac{k_{e}}{m}}=\sqrt{\frac{4 k}{m}}=2 \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$

and $\mathrm{f}=\frac{\omega}{2 \pi}=\frac{2}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}=\frac{1}{\pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$

</details>

### Q3. BITSAT 2020

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Level:* `3`

Frequency of oscillation is proportional to

<img src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/bitsat/2Fka4nbw_giuNK19bw_t9qgWuL0nJxRH2NdnHC2h4NI.original.fullsize.png">

**Options:**

- **(A)** $\sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}}$
- **(B)** $\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}}$
- **(C)** $\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}}$
- **(D)** $\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{m}}{3 \mathrm{k}}}$

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(A) $\sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}}$**

**Detailed Solution:**

<img src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/bitsat/fVXcn21iwp3NiK0FQADxaIUO2mU1h3GRfwNMO5PnGHg.original.fullsize.png">


Let mass is displaced towards left by $x$ then force on $\operatorname{mass}=-\mathrm{kx}-2 \mathrm{kx}=-3 \mathrm{kx}$

[negative sign is taken because force is opposite to the direction of motion]

$\begin{array}{l}

\Rightarrow \mathrm{F}=-3 \mathrm{kx}=-\mathrm{m} \omega^{2} \mathrm{x} \Rightarrow \omega=\sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}} \\

\mathrm{f}=\frac{\omega}{2 \pi}=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}}

\end{array}$

Thus it is propotional to $\sqrt{3 \mathrm{k} / \mathrm{m}}$

</details>

### Q6. BITSAT 2018

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Level:* `2`

The bob of simple pendulum is a spherical hollow ball filled with water. A plugged hole near the bottom of the oscillating bob get suddenly unplugged. During observation, till water is coming out, the time period of oscillation would

**Options:**

- **(A)** first increase and then decrease to the original value
- **(B)** first decrease and then increase to the original value
- **(C)** remain unchanged
- **(D)** increase towards a saturation value

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(A) first increase and then decrease to the original value**

**Detailed Solution:**

<p>The bob filled completely with water has its centre of mass at its centre. The time period of oscillation is</p><p><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>&#960;</mi><msqrt><mfrac><mi>l</mi><mi>g</mi></mfrac></msqrt></math></p><p>As the water starts coming out of the bob, its centre of mass shifts vertically downward and as a result, effective length of the pendulum increases and hence its period also increases. When the bob is empty, again its centre of mass appears at its centre and as a result, the period of oscillation again reaches to its original value.</p>

</details>

### Q7. BITSAT 2017

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Level:* `1`

Two simple pendulums of lengths <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>&#160;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo>&#160;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> respectively are given small displacement in one direction at the same time they will again be in the same sense when the pendulum of shorter length has completed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> oscillations. Then, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> is

**Options:**

- **(A)** <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math>
- **(B)** <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math>
- **(C)** <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math>
- **(D)** <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math>

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(C) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math>**

**Detailed Solution:**

<p>According to question</p><p><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math></p><p><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>&#8658;</mo><mo>&#160;</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#183;</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>&#960;</mi><msqrt><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mi>g</mi></mfrac></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced><mn>2</mn><mi>&#960;</mi><msqrt><mfrac><mn>20</mn><mi>g</mi></mfrac></msqrt></math></p><p><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math></p>

</details>
